header.userPrompt:
Add optional per-account nicknames (aliases) to bank statements.

## Problem
A user can hold several cards at the same bank. Statements only distinguish them by the last 4 digits, which is hard to tell apart. Let the user attach an optional, human-friendly nickname to an "account" and surface it in the UI.

## Concept — there is no account entity today
An "account" is the tuple (bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency) — the same 5-tuple key the overlap detection already uses in server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BankStatementDAO.scala (findOverlapping, overlappingStatementIds). The frontend currently derives an account grouping key in web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsLogic.scala (accountKey) and a display label in BankStatementsPage.scala (accountLabelOf). Do NOT introduce an account foreign key on bank_statement; the alias is a side lookup only.

## Data model
Add a new Play evolution (the next number after the latest file in server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/). Table `bank_account_alias`:
- id UUID NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY
- user_id UUID NOT NULL, FK -> users(user_id)
- bank_name TEXT NOT NULL
- product_type TEXT NOT NULL
- account_last4 TEXT NOT NULL
- currency TEXT NOT NULL
- alias TEXT NOT NULL      -- may be the empty string; never null
- created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
- updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
- UNIQUE (user_id, bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency)
- index on user_id

No CHECK constraints and no column DEFAULTs (app-level validation only, per repo conventions). The table stores ONLY the key tuple plus the alias — no other per-account settings.

## Behaviour
1. Ensure-at-confirm: in ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction's confirm path, inside the SAME transaction that creates the statement + rows (extend the repository method behind createConfirmedStatement), ensure a bank_account_alias row exists for the confirmed statement's tuple with an empty alias (""), only if one does not already exist. NEVER overwrite an existing alias.
2. Set-alias endpoint keyed by a STATEMENT id (not the tuple): the server loads the statement user-scoped, derives its tuple, and upserts the alias row (create if missing, update the alias if present). An empty alias is allowed and must be stored as-is. NEVER delete the row. Enforce a 60-character maximum app-side and return a validation error if exceeded. A statement id that is not the authenticated user's returns not found.
3. Reading: left-join the alias into the statement reads so each statement in the GetBankStatements list response and the GetBankStatement response carries its optional alias. A missing row or an empty alias string both mean "no nickname".

## Rendering
Keep the existing default label exactly as it is today (bank (product) dot-dot-dot-dot last4). When a non-empty alias exists, render it as `<alias> (<existing default label>)`. Put this in ONE shared label function that the list dropdown, the account selector, the per-account timeline, and the statement review header all call, so every surface agrees.

## Edit UI — both locations
- The statement review/detail header (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatementreview/).
- The list page's account selector (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsPage.scala).
In each, show the current alias and an inline control to edit it. Autofocus the input when the edit opens (useEffect + ref), and wrap it in an HTML form with onSubmit so Enter submits. Make the copy clear that the nickname applies to the whole account (every statement of that card), not to the single statement being viewed.

## Conventions (must follow)
- Tapir endpoint definitions live in lib/api/shared/ and are shared by both sides; wire controller -> thin action -> Anorm repository/DAO.
- Every DB query, read and write, includes WHERE user_id = ?. Every list query has an ORDER BY.
- Use Chimney (transformInto / into.transform) for case-class shape mapping instead of hand-copying fields.
- No external API calls in tests; follow docs/guide/testing.md.
- New API gets explicit length/count limits (the 60-char alias limit here).
- Frontend reachability: the edit control must be reachable and usable in the running UI, not just wired in the router.
- Public repository: NO personally identifying data anywhere in code, tests, comments, fixtures, or the PR text — no real bank names, account numbers, filenames, merchant names, or amounts. Use neutral placeholders.
- The PR description must NOT contain any claude.ai session link.

## Tests to add/adjust
- DAO: upsert create, upsert update, empty-alias stored as "", 60-char boundary accept + over-limit reject, and user-scoping (another user's tuple is isolated).
- Confirm flow: ensures an empty-alias row for the tuple and does not clobber an existing alias.
- Set-alias action: create, update, set-to-empty, over-length rejection, and wrong-user returns not found.
- The shared label function: alias set vs empty vs absent.

## Acceptance criteria
- A user can set, change, and clear (to empty) a nickname for an account from BOTH the statement review header and the list account selector; it persists and appears on every statement of that account.
- Confirming a statement ensures an empty-alias account row exists for its tuple without overwriting an existing alias.
- An alias longer than 60 characters is rejected with a validation error.
- All reads and writes are user-scoped; another user's statement id can neither set nor read an alias.
- The full test suite passes.

resultJson.description:
Users can hold several cards at the same bank, and statements only tell them apart by the last 4 digits. This epic lets a user give an "account" an optional nickname (alias) and shows it wherever the account is labelled. There is still no account entity. An account is the tuple (bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency), scoped to a user. That is the same key the overlap detection in BankStatementDAO already uses. The alias is stored in a new side table, `bank_account_alias` (evolution 14), keyed by that tuple with a UNIQUE constraint. `bank_statement` gets no foreign key.

On the server, confirming a draft also creates an empty-alias row for the statement's tuple in the same transaction (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), so an existing nickname is never overwritten. A new PUT endpoint keyed by a statement id loads that statement for the authenticated user, derives its tuple and upserts the alias. Empty strings are allowed and the row is never deleted. The action enforces a 60-character limit, and another user's statement id fails with "Bank statement not found". The statement reads (`BankStatementDAO.find`/`all`) LEFT JOIN the alias, so `GetBankStatements` and `GetBankStatement` each carry `accountAlias: Option[String]`. A missing row and "" both mean "no nickname".

On the frontend, one pure label function produces `<alias> (<bank> (<Product>) ••••<last4>)` when the alias is non-empty and the unchanged default label otherwise. The list dropdown, the per-account timeline, the delete dialog and the review header all call it. A shared inline editor (a form with onSubmit, and the input focused via useEffect + ref) is placed in the statement review header and next to the list page's account selector. Its copy makes clear that the nickname applies to every statement of that card. After a save, the UI updates every loaded statement with the same tuple.

tasks.title: Add bank_account_alias table, DAO and repository writes (ensure-at-confirm + upsert)
tasks.description:
Add evolution `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/14.sql` (header `-- !Ups`, no Downs, no DEFAULTs, no CHECKs, every constraint named). It creates `bank_account_alias(id UUID NOT NULL, user_id UUID NOT NULL, bank_name TEXT NOT NULL, product_type TEXT NOT NULL, account_last4 TEXT NOT NULL, currency TEXT NOT NULL, alias TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL)` with `CONSTRAINT bank_account_alias_id_pk PRIMARY KEY (id)`, `CONSTRAINT bank_account_alias_user_id_fk FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(user_id)`, `CONSTRAINT bank_account_alias_user_account_unique UNIQUE (user_id, bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency)` and `CREATE INDEX bank_account_alias_user_id_index ON bank_account_alias USING BTREE (user_id);`.

Add a model at `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/models/BankAccountAlias.scala`: the row case class, plus `BankAccountAlias.Key(bankName, productType, accountLast4, currency)`. Build a Key from `BankStatement.Metadata`, `BankStatement` or `BankStatementView` with Chimney `transformInto[BankAccountAlias.Key]`; extra source fields are ignored.

Add `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BankAccountAliasDAO.scala`. Use the Anorm `SQL"""…"""` interpolator and `user_id` in every WHERE:
- `ensureExists(id, userId, key, now)`: `INSERT … alias '' … ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT bank_account_alias_user_account_unique DO NOTHING`.
- `upsert(id, userId, key, alias, now)`: `INSERT … ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT … DO UPDATE SET alias = EXCLUDED.alias, updated_at = EXCLUDED.updated_at WHERE bank_account_alias.user_id = <userId>`. It never deletes.
- `find(userId, key): Option[BankAccountAlias]`.

In `BankStatementRepository.createConfirmedStatement`, inside the existing `withTransaction` and after `BankStatementDAO.create`, call `BankAccountAliasDAO.ensureExists`. Use a freshly generated id (`UuidCreator.getTimeOrderedEpoch()`) and `stmt.createdAt`, and keep the method signature unchanged.

Add `BankStatementRepository.setAccountAlias(bankStatementId, userId, alias, now): Future[Unit]` under `withTransaction`. It calls `BankStatementDAO.find(id, userId)`; if that returns None it throws `RuntimeException("Bank statement not found")`. Otherwise it derives the Key and calls `upsert`. Add `findAccountAlias(userId, key)` only if tests need a read path.

Tests go in `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepositorySpec.scala` (or a new `BankAccountAliasDAOSpec` under the same package using `RepositorySpec`):
- upsert creates a row.
- upsert updates the alias in place (same id, alias changed).
- An empty alias is stored as "".
- A 60-char alias is stored intact.
- One user's alias does not affect another user with the same tuple, and `find` for the other user returns None.
- `createConfirmedStatement` creates an empty-alias row for the tuple.
- A second confirm for the same tuple does not clobber an alias set in between.
- `setAccountAlias` with another user's statement id fails with "Bank statement not found" and writes nothing.

No DB constraint enforces the 60-char limit, so the over-limit rejection is tested at the endpoint in a later task. Use random users and neutral placeholder metadata (the existing `sampleStatementMetadata` "Test Bank"/"0000" is fine). Verify with `sbt "server/testOnly *BankStatementRepositorySpec"` (plus the new spec, if any).

tasks.title: Expose the account alias on statement reads (list + detail responses)
tasks.description:
Add `accountAlias: Option[String]` to `BankStatementView` (`server/.../repositories/models/BankStatementView.scala`; no default value). Then, in `BankStatementDAO.find` and `BankStatementDAO.all`, LEFT JOIN `bank_account_alias a ON a.user_id = bs.user_id AND a.bank_name = bs.bank_name AND a.product_type = bs.product_type AND a.account_last4 = bs.account_last4 AND a.currency = bs.currency`, select `a.alias`, and read it in `viewParser` with `get[Option[String]]("alias")`. Keep the existing `WHERE bs.user_id` and `ORDER BY`. The UNIQUE constraint guarantees at most one match, so the row count is unchanged.

Add `accountAlias: Option[String]` (no default) to `GetBankStatements.Response.BankStatement` and `GetBankStatement.Response` in `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/bankstatements/`. Pass the raw value through: a Some("") is not normalised on the server. While touching them, rewrite the hand-built mappings in `GetBankStatementsAction` and `GetBankStatementAction` with Chimney: `view.into[...]`, with `withFieldConst`/`withFieldComputed` for `documentStatus`, `overlappingStatementIds` and `statementRows`.

Fix every other construction site so it compiles:
- `web/.../bankstatements/BankStatementsLogic.mergePolled`: carry `updated.accountAlias`; consider Chimney there too.
- Test fixtures in `web/src/test/.../bankstatements/BankStatementListSpec.scala` and `BankStatementsLogicSpec.scala`.
- Test fixtures in `web/src/test/.../bankstatementreview/BankStatementRowActionsSpec.scala`, `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec.scala` (two sites) and `BankStatementReviewStoreSpec.scala`. Pass `accountAlias = None`.

Tests:
- Repository: `find`/`all` return None when no alias row exists, Some("") after confirm, and Some(value) after `setAccountAlias`. One alias set through statement A appears on statement B of the same tuple. A same-tuple alias of another user is not joined in.
- Controller (`server/src/test/scala/controllers/BankStatementsControllerSpec.scala`): `getBankStatements` and `getBankStatement` include the alias. Set it via `app.injector.instanceOf[BankStatementRepository].setAccountAlias`.
- `BankStatementsLogicSpec`: a mergePolled case keeps the polled alias.

Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile`, then testOnly the touched server specs and `web/testOnly *BankStatementsLogicSpec`.

tasks.title: Add the set-account-alias endpoint (keyed by statement id, 60-char limit)
tasks.description:
Add `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/bankstatements/SetAccountAlias.scala`, following the `ConfirmBankStatementRow` pattern: `Request(alias: String)`, `Response(alias: String)`, Play JSON formats and Tapir schemas named `SetAccountAliasRequest`/`SetAccountAliasResponse`. Add `val MaxAliasLength = 60` there so the frontend can reuse it.

In `BankStatementsEndpoints` add `setAccountAlias`: `baseEndpoint.put.in(path[UUID]("bankStatementId") / "account-alias").in(jsonBody[SetAccountAlias.Request]).in(userAuth).out(jsonBody[SetAccountAlias.Response]).errorOut(oneOf(HttpErrors.badRequest))`. Give it a summary saying the nickname applies to the whole account of that statement, and add it to `routes`.

In `ApiClient` add `def setBankStatementAccountAlias(bankStatementId: UUID, request: SetAccountAlias.Request): Future[SetAccountAlias.Response]`.

Add `server/.../actions/bankstatements/SetAccountAliasAction.scala`, a thin @Inject class with an implicit `Clock`. If `request.alias.length > SetAccountAlias.MaxAliasLength`, fail with `Future.failed(new RuntimeException("Nickname must be 60 characters or less"))`. Otherwise call `bankStatementRepository.setAccountAlias(id, userId, request.alias, clock.instant())`, log with `userId=` and the statement id (never the alias text), and return `Response(request.alias)`. Store the alias exactly as received, with no trimming.

Wire it in `controllers/BankStatementsController`: constructor injection, a private handler wrapped in `handleRequest`, and `BankStatementsEndpoints.setAccountAlias.serverLogic(...)` in `routes`.

Tests go in `server/src/test/scala/controllers/BankStatementsControllerSpec.scala` under `"PUT /bank-statements/:id/account-alias" should`:
- Create a nickname: it appears on `getBankStatement` and on every same-tuple statement in `getBankStatements`.
- Update it.
- Set it to "": it is stored and returned as Some("").
- Accept exactly 60 chars.
- Reject 61 chars with the validation message, leaving the stored alias unchanged.
- Another user's statement id returns "Bank statement not found" and changes nothing. Use `buildClient()` + `createVerifyLoginUser`.

Also add a confirm-flow test in `BankStatementDraftControllerSpec`: confirming a draft whose tuple already has an alias keeps that alias.

No action-level spec, per testing.md. Verify with `sbt "server/testOnly *BankStatementsControllerSpec *BankStatementDraftControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Shared account label function used by every account surface
tasks.description:
In `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsLogic.scala` add a pure function `accountLabel(bankName: String, productType: String, accountLast4: String, alias: Option[String]): String`. The default part must stay byte-identical to today's `s"$bankName (${BankStatementList.productLabel(productType)}) ••••$accountLast4"`. When `alias.exists(_.nonEmpty)` it returns `s"$alias ($default)"`.

Make `BankStatementList.accountLabelOf(s)` in `BankStatementsPage.scala` delegate to it with `s.accountAlias`. That keeps the account dropdown (`accounts`) and the delete dialog (`deleteSummaryLines`) on the shared function. The dropdown's `distinctBy(_._1)` takes the first statement per key, which is the newest created.

Add a small heading above the per-account timeline cards (e.g. `Statements · <label>`) that calls the same function for the selected account's representative statement.

In `bankstatementreview/BankStatementReviewHeader.scala`, render an `Account: <label>` line using `BankStatementsLogic.accountLabel(stmt.bankName, stmt.productType, stmt.accountLast4, stmt.accountAlias)`. Keep the existing metadata line's other parts (bank, type, currency, period); drop or replace only the duplicated `Account: ••••last4` part.

Also add these pure helpers to `BankStatementsLogic`, for use by the editor task:
- `accountRepresentative(stmts, accountKey: Option[String]): Option[GetBankStatements.Response.BankStatement]`: the newest-created statement of the selected account, matching the dropdown.
- `applyAlias(stmts, of: GetBankStatements.Response.BankStatement, alias: String)`: sets `accountAlias = Some(alias)` on every statement with the same (bankName, productType, accountLast4, currency) and leaves others untouched.

Tests in `web/src/test/.../bankstatements/BankStatementsLogicSpec.scala` (and/or `BankStatementListSpec.scala`), with method-only descriptions and neutral placeholders such as "Example Bank", "1111" and "Travel card" (never real bank names):
- `accountLabel` with alias set, with Some("") and with None: the last two equal the default label.
- `accountLabelOf` uses the alias.
- `accountRepresentative` picks the newest statement.
- `applyAlias` updates same-tuple statements only, including one where the currency differs.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementsLogicSpec *BankStatementListSpec"` (Node 24 must be on PATH).

tasks.title: Inline nickname editor in the review header and the list account selector
tasks.description:
Create one reusable component, e.g. `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/AccountAliasEditor.scala`, with `Props(currentAlias: String, onSave: String => Future[Unit])`. The callers supply the API call. Model its UI state as one ADT in a single `Hooks.useState`, e.g. `enum EditState { case Closed; case Editing(draft: String, error: Option[String]); case Saving(draft: String) }`. Do not use parallel flags.

Closed: show the current nickname (or "No nickname") and an "Edit nickname" button.

Editing: render `form(onSubmit := { e => e.preventDefault(); save() })`, wrapping an MUI outlined TextField and Save/Cancel buttons. The Save button is `type=submit`, so Enter submits.
- Focus the input with `Hooks.useRef` plus `SafeHooks.useEffect(<string key that changes when editing opens>)` calling `.focus()`. Pass the ref via the TextField's `inputRef`, or find the input element under a wrapping ref if the facade lacks `inputRef`.
- Show helper text such as "Applies to every statement of this card, not just this one" and the char count against `SetAccountAlias.MaxAliasLength`. Disable Save when over the limit; the server stays authoritative.
- Trim before sending; sending "" clears the nickname.
- On failure, return to Editing with the server error message.

Review header: `BankStatementReviewHeader.Props` gains `onSaveAlias: String => Future[Unit]`, and the header renders the editor next to the `Account:` label. In `BankStatementReviewContent`, build it as `client.setBankStatementAccountAlias(stmt.id, SetAccountAlias.Request(a)).map(r => store.setAccountAlias(r.alias))`. Add `setAccountAlias(alias: String)` to `BankStatementReviewStore`; it patches `$statement` only when Loaded. Update the store's doc comment, which currently says `$statement` never changes once loaded. Cover the setter in `BankStatementReviewStoreSpec`.

List page: in `BankStatementList` (in `BankStatementsPage.scala`), render the editor next to the Account select for `BankStatementsLogic.accountRepresentative(localStmts, selectedAccount)`. Key the editor by the selected account so switching accounts resets it. On save, call the API with the representative's id and then `setLocalStmts(cur => BankStatementsLogic.applyAlias(cur, rep, r.alias))`, using the functional updater. Labels in the dropdown, the timeline heading and the delete dialog then refresh.

Both controls must be visible and usable in the running UI; the existing routes already reach both pages. Add a jsdom render test only if it guards a specific runtime failure (testing.md RULE-TE-010). Otherwise extract any non-trivial logic (e.g. a `canSave(draft)`/length check) into a pure function and unit-test it. Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewStoreSpec *BankStatementsLogicSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/api/shared/: Tapir endpoints and request/response models shared by the server and Scala.js.
  - Endpoints: lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/endpoints/BankStatementsEndpoints.scala (`baseEndpoint` = `endpoint.in("bank-statements").tag(...).errorOut(errorResponseErrorOut)`; each endpoint uses `.in(userAuth).out(jsonBody[...]).errorOut(oneOf(HttpErrors.badRequest))`). Every endpoint must also be added to the `routes` list at the bottom.
  - Models: lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/bankstatements/*. Pattern: an `object X { case class Request; case class Response; implicit Format via Json.format; implicit Schema via Schema.derived[..].name(Schema.SName("XRequest")) }` — see ConfirmBankStatementRow.scala.
  - Client: lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/ApiClient.scala. A concrete class; methods look like `handleRequest(BankStatementsEndpoints.x, (id, request, dummyUserId))`.
  - The repo uses no Tapir `Validator`s. Length limits are app-side checks in actions that throw `RuntimeException("<Field> must be N characters or less")`; see actions/merchants/CreateMerchantAction.scala.
- server/: Play backend. The flow is controller → thin action → repository → DAO.
  - controllers/BankStatementsController.scala: actions are constructor-injected, each handler is wrapped in `handleRequest { for { userId <- userIdF; r <- action(...) } yield Right(r) }`, and the `routes` list holds `Endpoint.serverLogic(handler)`.
  - controllers/package.scala `errorHandler` turns any NonFatal exception into `Left(ErrorResponse(ex.getMessage))` (HTTP 400). "Not found" and validation errors are therefore just RuntimeException messages. The existing not-found text is exactly "Bank statement not found".
  - Actions: server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/. ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction calls `bankStatementRepository.createConfirmedStatement(stmt, metadata, rows, extractionInfo, job)`. GetBankStatementsAction and GetBankStatementAction build their responses by hand from `BankStatementView`; convert them to Chimney when you touch them (`import io.scalaland.chimney.dsl.*`). Chimney ignores extra source fields; use `withFieldConst`/`withFieldComputed` for the rest.
  - Repository: server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepository.scala (`@Inject()(database: Database)(implicit ec: DatabaseExecutionContext)`). Each method is `Future { database.withConnection|withTransaction { implicit conn => DAO... } }`. Several DB calls together must use `withTransaction`. A user-scoped pre-read (`BankStatementDAO.find(id, userId)`) that throws "Bank statement not found" is the established pattern (setRowExpenseId, ignoreRow, …).
  - DAO: server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BankStatementDAO.scala. It uses the Anorm `SQL"""…${v}"""` interpolator with `${id.toString}::UUID` casts. `find(id, userId)` and `all(userId)` return `BankStatementView` via the private `viewParser` (bs JOIN document d, LEFT JOIN row counts); `all` has `ORDER BY bs.created_at DESC, bs.id`. `findOverlapping` and `overlappingStatementIds` show the account-tuple matching: bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency. ON CONFLICT is an existing pattern (MerchantDAO, CategoryDAO, DocumentDAO).
  - Models: repositories/models/BankStatement.scala (BankStatement, BankStatement.Create, BankStatement.Metadata(bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd)) and repositories/models/BankStatementView.scala.
  - Evolutions: server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/1..13.sql, so the new file is 14.sql. Style is `-- !Ups`, UPPER-CASE SQL, explicitly named constraints (`<table>_id_pk`, `<table>_user_id_fk`, `<table>_..._unique`), and `CREATE INDEX <table>_user_id_index ON <table> USING BTREE (user_id);`. There are no Downs, DEFAULTs or CHECKs. Add only one evolution per PR, and never edit existing ones.
- web/: Scala.js + Slinky + MUI 5.
  - web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsPage.scala holds `BankStatementsPage` (AsyncComponent fetch) and `BankStatementList`. Inside `BankStatementList`:
    - `productLabel`, `accountKeyOf` (bank~product~last4; NO currency, used in URL `?account=` and by BankStatementReviewLogic.backToListPath, so do not change it), `accountLabelOf` (`s"${bankName} (${productLabel(productType)}) ••••${last4}"` — keep it byte-identical as the default label) and `metadataLine`.
    - `localStmts` state (`Hooks.useState(props.stmts.data)`, re-synced from props by a `stmtsKey` effect).
    - `accounts = localStmts.map(s => accountKeyOf(s) -> accountLabelOf(s)).distinctBy(_._1)`, `selectedAccount = BankStatementsLogic.selectedAccountKey(urlQuery.account, localStmts)`, and the Account `mui.TextField.select` around line 494.
  - web/.../bankstatements/BankStatementsLogic.scala holds pure logic with no React: accountKey, timeline, mergePolled (builds GetBankStatements.Response.BankStatement by hand from GetBankStatement.Response), removeStatement, deleteSummaryLines (uses accountLabelOf).
  - web/.../bankstatementreview/:
    - BankStatementReviewHeader.scala: Props(statement: GetBankStatement.Response, rowCount, regenerateDisabled, onRegenerate); a private statementMetadataLine shows `Account: ••••last4`.
    - BankStatementReviewContent.scala renders the header at around line 206 inside `renderLoaded(stmt, rowActions)`; client = `props.ctx.api.client`, `implicit ec = props.ctx.executionContext`.
    - BankStatementReviewStore.scala: monix `Var`s; `$statement: Var[Loadable[GetBankStatement.Response]]`; Loadable lives in BankStatementReviewLogic.
  - Hooks: use `net.wiringbits.core.SafeHooks.{useEffect,useMemo,useCallback}` with String dependency keys, never raw Hooks deps. Use the functional updater (`setX(cur => ...)`). Put mutually exclusive UI state in one ADT in one useState. Forms follow the MerchantsPage.scala pattern: `import slinky.web.html.{form, onSubmit}`; `form(onSubmit := { e => e.preventDefault(); ... })(...)`. There is no existing useRef+focus example; the spec requires useEffect + ref (not just `.autoFocus(true)`).
  - Every reused React element must be a `def`, not a `val`. Object-level vals hold only plain JS literals.

CONVENTIONS / GOTCHAS
- Every SQL read and write includes `WHERE user_id = ?`, and every list query has an ORDER BY. The unique key (user_id, bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency) makes the LEFT JOIN into statement reads return at most one row; join on user_id as well.
- Upserts rely on the DB constraint (`ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT bank_account_alias_user_account_unique`), never a check-then-write. "Ensure" = DO NOTHING (never clobbers); "set" = DO UPDATE SET alias, updated_at. Never delete alias rows. An empty string is a valid stored value and is distinct from no row, but the UI treats both as "no nickname". The server stores the alias exactly as sent (no trim); the frontend trims before sending.
- Length/shape validation (60 chars) lives in the action. Ownership comes from the user-scoped statement lookup inside the repository transaction. Put the `MaxAliasLength = 60` constant in the shared API model so both sides use it.
- No default parameter values on domain models or meaningful function params (reviewer rule). Adding `accountAlias` to BankStatementView and the API response models forces every construction site to be updated. Server: the two Get actions. Web main: BankStatementsLogic.mergePolled. Web tests: BankStatementListSpec, BankStatementsLogicSpec (2 sites), BankStatementRowActionsSpec, BankStatementReviewLogicSpec (2), BankStatementReviewStoreSpec.
- Logs on user-scoped operations include `userId=$userId`; never log the alias text. Comments explain intent, not the change.
- Tests:
  - Repository/DAO specs extend `net.wiringbits.core.RepositorySpec` with `utils.RepositoryUtils` (`withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`, `createUser()`, `createBankStatement(userId)`, `sampleStatementMetadata` = "Test Bank"/credit/USD/"0000"). `RepositoryUtils.createStatement` writes via BankStatementDAO directly, so it creates NO alias row; `createConfirmedStatement` does.
  - Controller specs (`controllers/BankStatementsControllerSpec.scala`, `BankStatementDraftControllerSpec.scala`) extend PlayPostgresSpec. Use `withApiClient { implicit client => ... }`, `client.currentUser.futureValue.id`, and `createBankStatement(userId, metadata)` / `createBankStatementWithRows` (these go through createConfirmedStatement, so an empty alias row exists). Set up a second user with `val client2 = buildClient(); createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator)(using executionContext, client2).futureValue`, and check failures with `.expectError` (returns the error message). Use `app.injector.instanceOf[BankStatementRepository]` for direct setup.
  - Don't add action-level specs; controller tests cover actions. Test descriptions name only the method or behaviour, never the type. Use random/unique data per test (shared Postgres container). Nothing may call an external API.
  - Web tests are pure AnyWordSpec unit tests; avoid jsdom unless it guards a known runtime crash.
- Public repo: no PII. Use neutral placeholders (e.g. "Example Bank", "Test Bank", "1111", "Travel card"). Existing web fixtures contain a real bank name; don't copy it into new tests. Keep the PR description free of any claude.ai session link.
- Build/verify:
  - `CI=true sbt Test/compile` (-Werror).
  - Targeted `sbt "server/testOnly *Spec"` / `sbt "web/testOnly *Spec"`.
  - Web tests need Node 24 on PATH; the default shell node is v16 and yarn install fails.
  - BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec is known-flaky; ignore it.
  - Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing. Don't run the full `sbt test` per task.
- Known limitation to keep: the frontend account grouping key omits currency while the alias tuple includes it. The list editor targets the selected group's newest-created statement (the same one whose label the dropdown shows), and `applyAlias` updates only statements whose full 4-tuple matches.

findings.title: SetAccountAlias.Request.alias has no declared max length in the API definition

reason.text: I tried the suggested `Validator.maxLength(MaxAliasLength)` on the Request and Response schemas, and it breaks the required behaviour. The shared sttp ApiClient checks the schema before it sends anything, so a 61-character nickname never reaches the server. The caller gets "Exception when sending request: PUT …" instead of "Nickname must be 60 characters or less". I confirmed this with the over-length controller test, which failed with exactly that message. The repo's convention is no Tapir Validators: length limits are checked in the action and fail with a RuntimeException message, as in CreateMerchantAction. The limit is still declared once in lib/api/shared as `SetAccountAlias.MaxAliasLength` and enforced on the server before anything is stored. I reverted the change, so SetAccountAlias.scala is back to its original content and nothing else changed.

id.name: Task: Shared account label function used by every account surface

findings.title: Account identity encoded twice with different fields (accountKey omits currency, applyAlias includes it)

reason.text: The task spec says to keep this as a known limitation. accountKey/accountKeyOf must not change because the `?account=` URLs and BankStatementReviewLogic.backToListPath use them. applyAlias must match on the server's 4-field alias key, or it would show nicknames the server never stored. The existing applyAlias test already covers the case of the same key with a different currency. I added a comment on accountKey that explains the deliberate currency collapse.

findings.title: Account grouping key omits currency but alias/applyAlias key includes it, so one dropdown account can show a wrong or inconsistent nickname

reason.text: Same issue as I3.1, and the spec deliberately keeps it as a known limitation. Adding currency to accountKey would break the existing `?account=` URLs and backToListPath, which the spec forbids changing. Making applyAlias use the 3-field key would put the UI out of step with the server's 4-field alias row. I documented the choice in a comment on accountKey.

findings.title: Account grouping key omits currency but alias is per (bank, product, last4, currency)

reason.text: Same issue as I3.1 and I4.1, and the spec deliberately keeps it as a known limitation: the 3-field grouping key must stay, and applyAlias must mirror the server's 4-field key. I documented this in a comment on accountKey; the rest is out of scope.
